idea.body: A triangle's three angles always add up to 180 degrees. If a rover's support brace has angles of 50 and 70 degrees, the third is 180 minus 50 minus 70, which is 60 degrees. Extending one side past a vertex makes an exterior angle. That exterior angle always equals the sum of the two interior angles that are not next to it. An isosceles triangle has two equal sides, and the angles across from those sides, its base angles, are also equal. An equilateral triangle has three equal sides, so all three angles equal 60 degrees. These facts let you find a missing angle without ever measuring it.

figure.alt: A triangle with angles 50 degrees, 70 degrees, and an unknown angle.

workedExample.prompt: A kite frame is an isosceles triangle with a vertex angle of 40 degrees. Find each base angle.
steps: The two base angles of an isosceles triangle are equal.
All three angles add up to 180 degrees, so the two base angles together equal 180 - 40 = 140 degrees.
Split that evenly between the two equal base angles: 140 / 2 = 70.

ways.when: Use this when two sides of the triangle are equal and you know the vertex angle.
steps: A trellis brace is an isosceles triangle with a vertex angle of 56 degrees.

All three angles add to 180: 56 plus x plus x equals 180.

ways.name: The exterior angle shortcut
ways.when: Use this when a side is extended and you want the outside angle, without finding the third interior angle first.
steps: A kite frame has interior angles of 37 degrees and 65 degrees at two corners.
One side is extended past the third corner, making an exterior angle there.
The exterior angle always equals the sum of the two angles not next to it.
Add the two remote angles: 37 plus 65 is 102.
